newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UM studies Sibeka delisting - paper.
newsitem.headline: UM studies Sibeka delisting - paper.

text.p: Union Miniere (UM), the Belgian non-ferrous metals group, is studying the purchase of the 1.8 percent of the share capital of its synthetic diamond subsidiary Sibeka it does not already own, Belgian paper L'Echo said.
Following the so-called squeeze-out operation Sibeka might be delisted from the second market of the Brussels bourse, the paper said in its Friday edition.
UM raised its stake in Sibeka via two recent public offers to 78.6 percent.
De Beers, the South African diamond giant, holds 19.6 percent, leaving 1.8 percent still in public hands.
Union Miniere has said De Beers will hold on to its Sibeka stake to maintain its links with UM's holding company SGB in the diamond sector.

Sibeka operates in the natural diamond and synthetic abrasives sector and has a 50 percent stake in the Megapode Group, the world's leading producer of synthetic diamonds which is managed by De Beers.
UM had a difficult time with Sibeka in 1996, when Sibeka contributed a net loss of 125 million francs compared with a net profit of 594 million francs in 1995.
